evidence.key_observation: A single bus write of 0x4000_22BB to the read-only STATUS register at offset 0x14 moved CONTROL at offset 0x10 from rx=aa tx=11 spien=1 to rx=bb tx=22 spien=0 sw_rst=1, on one unmodified spi_host_reg_top driven only through its ports. The byte values 0xbb and 0x22 appear in no earlier transaction, so the new contents can only have come from the STATUS write. intg_err_o stayed low through that transaction, so the spurious-write-enable checker did not report it. Correcting the qualifier in a scratch copy and rerunning the same bench yields checks=8 fails=0 witness_hits=0.
evidence.structural_audit: 42 of 42 gates hold (proof/logs/run.log). src/spi_host/rtl/spi_host_reg_top.sv:2019 qualifies CONTROL's write-enable as (~&{~addr_hit[4], ~addr_hit[5]}) & reg_we & !reg_error, which is addr_hit[4] | addr_hit[5]. Index 4 decodes CONTROL, index 5 decodes STATUS.
evidence.sibling_census: The file contains 13 write-enable assignments (measured 13). 12 of them use the single form addr_hit[N] & reg_we & !reg_error (measured 12), so exactly 1 departs from it (measured 1). The NAND-of-inverted-address-hits construct appears exactly once in the entire tree (measured 1). The hand-written comment 'Register update qualification.' sits on that one assignment and appears in no other register block in the tree (measured 1 file), while the generator's own section comment for the block, 'Generate write-enables', is the idiom shared with other register blocks.
evidence.read_only_contract: STATUS has no write-enable of its own anywhere in the file (measured 0) and is generated as a stored hardware-driven register, R[status]: V(False). The register spec declares it swaccess ro and hwaccess hwo (src/spi_host/data/spi_host.hjson:136-137), so software has no legitimate write path to it at all.
evidence.countermeasure_blindness: At :2122 the checker vector has reg_we_check[4] = control_we and reg_we_check[5] = 1'b0, feeding a 15-wide onehot check whose error output is the block's latched integrity error (:94). On a STATUS write exactly one vector bit is asserted, so the onehot condition is satisfied and no error is raised. 2 checker bits are tied low (measured 2), the two read-only registers. The other one, RXDATA at index 10, is the control case: its address hit appears in no write-enable at all (measured 0) and is used 4 times for decoder, permit check, read-enable and readback. The STATUS hit is used 4 times as well, but one of those is a write-enable rather than a read-enable (measured 1 inside write-enables).
evidence.what_lands_in_control: The write data is the raw bus word: bits 7:0 to rx_watermark, 15:8 to tx_watermark, 29 to output_en, 30 to sw_rst, 31 to spien (:2022-2030). All 5 CONTROL fields take their enable from that single qualifier (measured 5), so they move together. sw_rst and spien are both consumed by src/spi_host/rtl/spi_host.sv, so a spurious update has an effect beyond the register file.
evidence.directed_simulation: checks=8 fails=3 witness_hits=1, all five covers hit (proof/logs/sim.log). Controls: CONTROL holds its reset values with intg_err low; a direct CONTROL write lands (rx=aa tx=11 spien=1), which is the anti-vacuity check without which every 'CONTROL unchanged' assertion would pass for the wrong reason; a CONFIGOPTS write leaves CONTROL alone, establishing that address decoding is otherwise sound; STATUS reads back with hresp=0, so the address is genuinely mapped. Violating: the STATUS write modifies CONTROL; it sets sw_rst and clears spien in the same transaction; and intg_err_o stays low while it does.
evidence.negative_control: 16 of 16 gates hold (proof/logs/negative_control.log). A scratch copy rewrites :2019-2020 into assign control_we = addr_hit[4] & reg_we & !reg_error, gated at exactly 1 line added and 2 removed by difflib, with the audited source verified untouched. The same unmodified bench then reports checks=8 fails=0 witness_hits=0 and result=NOT_THE_AUDITED_SIGNATURE: the STATUS write no longer modifies CONTROL, no longer sets sw_rst or clears spien, while the anti-vacuity control still shows a direct CONTROL write landing. Transcripts from that run are in proof/negative_control_run/, outside proof/logs/, because a run on corrected RTL legitimately ends in a non-pass verdict.
evidence.containment: Asserting rst_ni low restores CONTROL to rx=7f sw_rst=0 spien=0, so the injected state is a register value that a reset clears, not a permanent condition.
evidence.reach: spi_host is delivered as a standalone block in this tree: no design file instantiates it (measured 0, the only instantiation being the block's own testbench, measured 1) and it does not appear in the SoC register map header, so reach is stated at its own boundary. That boundary is an AHB-Lite slave port, so the adversary is any master on the bus the block is attached to. STATUS's offset is a published parameter of the block's register package and the block ships a register description, so the address is part of its documented programming interface.

security_impact: A write to an address the register spec declares software-read-only commits a full 32-bit update into CONTROL, and the countermeasure meant to catch exactly that kind of out-of-bounds write-enable does not fire. Two consequences follow. An agent whose access policy permits STATUS but not CONTROL obtains sw_rst and spien, so it can reset the SPI host or take it offline from an address that is supposed to be inert, and can shift both FIFO watermarks so firmware is told the FIFOs need service at the wrong times. Separately, the same path fires for benign firmware: a driver that writes STATUS, which the contract says is harmless, silently corrupts CONTROL instead, and because intg_err_o stays low nothing upstream is informed. The exposure is bounded by reset, which restores CONTROL's reset values, so this is a corruptible register state rather than a permanent condition.
non_findings: Not a claim that software gains a write capability it entirely lacks. CONTROL is SwAccessRW at its own address, so the finding is that the write is reachable from an address where it must not be, and that it is silent.
Not a claim about the SoC address map. No design file in this tree instantiates spi_host, so no statement is made about which agents sit on its bus.
Not a fault-injection finding. No glitch, no physical access and no debug state is involved; the path is a plain bus write.
The onehot checker is not itself broken. It is satisfied because exactly one vector bit asserts, which is the point: the defect is invisible to it by construction rather than by a checker bug.
No claim that STATUS's own contents are corrupted. STATUS remains hardware-driven and read-only; it is the address, not the register, that is borrowed.
proof_integrity: One unmodified spi_host_reg_top, instantiated with ports only. No hierarchical reference into the DUT, no force, no assertion inside the DUT relied upon for any verdict.
Hardware-side inputs held at zero for the whole run, so no hardware path could be blamed for a CONTROL field changing.

Check polarity is fixed by convention: every check states the behaviour the design is supposed to have, so a failing check is the defect speaking. The pass gate demands checks=8, fails=3 and witness_hits=1 together, so a bench that silently stopped exercising something cannot report a pass.
A corrected qualifier produces a distinct verdict, result=NOT_THE_AUDITED_SIGNATURE, rather than a pass or a failure, so the two outcomes cannot be confused.
The witness payload uses byte values that appear in no earlier transaction, so the observation is not attributable to any prior write.
The intg_err check is conditional on the witness having fired, so it cannot pass vacuously on RTL where nothing was written out of bounds.
Censuses are computed and are written so as not to name the audited signal, so a pattern that failed to match reports a wrong count and fails a gate instead of passing silently.
The negative-control patch is size-gated with difflib at exactly 1 line added and 2 removed, and re-verifies that the audited source still contains the defect afterwards.
The scratch copy is written under proof/scratch and removed before packaging; nothing in the audited tree is modified by any script.

One assertion inside the DUT's own submodules, AssertConnected_A in caliptra_prim_onehot_check, fires once at 1ps in every run. It checks that the block's instantiating parent bound the count-error alert, which happens above spi_host_reg_top and is therefore absent in any block-level compile, so it is an artifact of compiling the block alone rather than a result. The sim script passes -assert filter_names=AssertConnected_A intending to suppress it; VCS reports it anyway, so it is visible in the transcripts. It is inert with respect to every verdict: it appears identically in the audited and the negative-control runs, the simulation runs to its own $finish in both, and the verdict is computed only from the bench's own check counters and covers, not from any assertion inside the DUT.
residual_uncertainty: The severity depends on which agents can reach the block's AHB port, and that cannot be settled in this tree because no design file instantiates spi_host. If every agent that can write STATUS can also write CONTROL, the integrity gain is small and the finding reduces to the silent-corruption path plus the countermeasure gap. The availability effect of sw_rst and spien is read from their consumers in spi_host.sv rather than simulated at block level.
